requests.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Make ONE transparent 2D game obstacle for a 120x120 wu test map. FIRST image is its unique fixed footprint mask: preserve its boundary, proportions and orientation. SECOND image is the same family's earlier art, THIRD is the SMALL sprite used as a shared detail-scale reference. Content: broken ancient paving, brown dirt, muted blue-gray shallow rain puddles and sparse moss. The NEW footprint measures 13.99 by 4.67 world units. CRITICAL: the whole footprint is larger, but individual objects remain at the SAME WORLD SCALE as on small footprints. Stone slabs mostly 0.8-1.4 world units wide, loose stones 0.15-0.35 wu, moss tufts 0.2 wu. Add more slabs to cover a larger footprint; never enlarge the slabs. Infer pixel sizes as feature-world-size / footprint-world-size; for example a 0.65 wu diamond is only 4.6% of this footprint's width. Cover large areas by adding more same-sized elements and terrain, never by enlarging a copied miniature. Preserve angled top-down perspective, painterly matte storybook palette, deep plum outer contour. All ground-level; human pursuers cross while player is excluded. Transparent outside mask, no exterior glow/vignette/shadow, no walls, buildings, people or text.
